response: Yes, polymorphisms in the beta-adrenergic receptor (ADRB) encoding genes may play a role in the development of transient tachypnea of the newborn (TTN). Research suggests that genetic variations in the ADRB2 gene, which codes for the beta-2 adrenergic receptor, may influence the risk of TTN. These polymorphisms can affect the function of the beta-2 adrenergic receptor, leading to altered responses to catecholamines and potentially contributing to the pathophysiology of TTN. However, more studies are needed to fully understand the relationship between ADRB polymorphisms and TTN.
